SCUG employees, not being civil servants, may invoke Article 199 against a transfer, but that settles only the forum: no one has a vested right to a particular station, and interference lies solely for breach of statutory tenure or rule, or mala fides on the record. Refusal of the main relief, however, does not bar a direction to the authority to post the employee to a post that lawfully exists.

2026-shc-suk-1894.excerpt: A Nikahnama entry showing dower as prompt proves the obligation, not its payment. Section 10(4) of the Act of 1964 allows restoration only of dower actually received, and its relinquishment is itself the Zar-e-Khula. The
2026-shc-suk-1894.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1894.full_text:
Const. P. 144/2023 (S.B.) Mst. Amna Shaikh V/S Imran Ahmed Shaikh & another
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A Nikahnama entry showing dower as prompt proves the obligation, not its payment. Section 10(4) of the Act of 1964 allows restoration only of dower actually received, and its relinquishment is itself the Zar-e-Khula. The Qanun-e-Shahadat being excluded by section 17, a wife's consistent account of an ordinary dowry list proves it and cannot be reduced by the Court's own estimate of her family's means.

2026-shc-suk-1915.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
2026-shc-suk-1915.full_text:

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

An employee of a Local Council, though a public servant under Section 151 of the Act of 2013, is not a civil servant; but Rule 26 of the Rules of 2017 carried the benefit of Rule 11-A to him mutatis mutandis until 18.10.2024. After Muhammad Jalal, no fresh entitlement survives; a right accrued on a death before that date stands preserved alike for both classes, with limitation running from majority where the dependant was a minor.

2026-shc-suk-1913.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 173/2023 (S.B.) Late Alllah Dino Through his LRs V/S Muhammad Zafar & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A registered thirty-year-old deed is presumed genuine under Articles 85(5), 100 and 129(e) QSO, 1984. The burden shifts to its beneficiary only once the challenger goes beyond bare denial. Its cancellation is governed by Article 91 of the Limitation Act, and forgery gives no immunity from time. A reversing decree that ignores those presumptions, awards possession and mesne profits without findings, and binds co-heirs never impleaded cannot stand. Non-joinder calls for impleadment, not dismissal.

2026-shc-suk-1912.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

R.A (Civil Revision) 192/2018 (S.B.) Muhammad Tagial Maitlo V/S Wazeer Ali & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

An oral sale agreement, unproved for want of particulars and independent evidence, gives no right to cancel a registered deed, section 39 aside, because it creates no interest in land. A co-defendant's admission through an attorney who never deposed cannot displace the deed's presumption. The purchaser for value in good faith is protected by section 27(b) unless notice is brought home to him.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

In a suit under Section 8 of the Act of 1877, the manner of dispossession is no ingredient of relief, where title stands proved, the case turns on the identity of the plot on the ground, which the court may settle by a local investigation of its own motion under Section 75 read with Order XXVI Rule 9 CPC. A Revenue Officer who, under the guise of correcting the record, adjudicates a stranger's title acts beyond his power and an order so made against a man long dead and without notice to his recorded heirs is a nullity that section 172 does not protect. 2026-shc-lar-1941.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
2026-shc-lar-1941.full_text:
Const. P. 326/2026 (D.B.) Irshad Khatoon V/S The P.O Sindh & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

Every limb of section 2(f) of the Act of 2014, as it stood in 2015, is tied to terrorism, and a constable killed by negligent driving, though on duty, falls outside it; the substitution of 2023 enlarges the class of beneficiaries, is substantive and prospective, and its "act of violence" imports intentional force. Entitlement crystallises on the date of death, and declarations wrongly made in other cases found no claim, Article 25 knowing no negative equality.

Const. P. 1033/2026 (S.B.) JAWAD AHMED S/O MUHAMMAD ALI V/S MST SALMA D/O FAREED AHMED & OTHERS
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri(Author)

Mere disagreement with the appreciation of evidence or the conclusions reached by the Courts below does not furnish a ground for interference under Article 199 of the Constitution. The Honourable Supreme Court has consistently emphasized that the legislative scheme governing family disputes must be respected and that constitutional jurisdiction cannot be invoked to circumvent the statutory restriction on further appeals. Consequently, the petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed in limine

const-p-6736-2026-d-b-altaf-karim-others.full_text:
Const. P. 6736/2026 (D.B.) Altaf Karim & others V/S Idrees Sattar Agar & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri(Author)

It is well settled that availability of an alternate remedy does not constitute an absolute bar to constitutional jurisdiction; nevertheless, where an adequate and efficacious remedy exists before the competent forum, constitutional jurisdiction is not ordinarily exercised unless exceptional circumstances, such as patent want of jurisdiction, manifest illegality or infringement of a fundamental right incapable of adequate redress through the ordinary remedy, are demonstrated. No such exceptional circumstance has been shown in the present case. Consequently, the Constitution Petition, being misconceived in the present form, is dismissed in limine.
